title: Shopify API Guide: How the 5 APIs Work (2026)
summary: Shopify API access depends on your app type, scopes and rate limits. See what requests your app can make and how to troubleshoot common errors.
body_markdown:
## Call the Shopify API without code in Activepieces


When your job is order, product or customer automation triggered by a store event, Activepieces fits, and the free plan covers it: unlimited flows and 1,000 credits a month, with a run costing 1 credit however many steps it has.


It handles the connection, the trigger and the request plumbing so you describe the flow instead of coding it.


Even a version you pinned and reviewed has to be maintained somewhere, and here the integration is where that upkeep sits, not in your own script.


Start with a free tier or self-hosted install, a custom app on your own store, and one token. That covers a lot of small-shop work: tagging orders, notifying a packer, adding customers to a mailing list.


### Connect a store with an access token


Create a custom app in your Shopify admin, grant it only the scopes the flow needs, and copy the Admin API access token it gives you.


Paste the store domain and that token into the Shopify connection in Activepieces; on the free plan, that connection can feed as many flows as you build, since flows are unlimited on every plan.


If the scope list is narrow, a leaked connection can read orders but not touch products, so choose it deliberately.


The Ultimate plan lists secret managers alongside SCIM, custom RBAC and audit logs, and with it that token can sit in your own secret manager instead of Activepieces' database.


The token is the same credential you'd use calling Shopify directly, which matters in the next step.


### Trigger on Shopify orders and call GraphQL


Start the flow with a Shopify trigger such as a new order. Activepieces, which carries 750 integrations in its MIT-licensed core, registers the webhook for you, so you skip building a receiving endpoint and verifying its signature.


Then add the Shopify action steps you need. For an endpoint the integration doesn't cover, add a custom HTTP request step and send the same token in the Shopify access-token header, with a GraphQL query in the body.


Take from it that both branches authenticate identically, so you never need a second credential.


Write code instead when the job is a heavy bulk sync, where you want direct control over query cost and throttling.


Do the same when you're building a public app that other merchants install. Those need OAuth, review and scale that a flow tool isn't meant to carry.
